Key terms: Frequency (pitch, Hz), Amplitude (loudness), Wavelength (distance between two compressions or two rarefactions).

Echo: Reflection of sound off a hard surface, heard after the original sound.

questions.q: Using which of the following processes can one separate a solute from its solution?
questions.theory:
Acids: All acids contain Hydrogen (H⁺ ions); turn blue litmus red; pH < 7. Common: HCl (stomach), Citric acid (citrus fruits), Acetic/Ethanoic acid (vinegar).
Bases/Alkalis: Turn red litmus blue; pH > 7; release OH⁻ ions. Common: NaOH (caustic soda), baking soda (sodium bicarbonate, mild base).
pH scale: 0–14; 7 = neutral (pure water); below 7 = acidic; above 7 = basic.
Reaction types: Oxidation = loss of electrons/gain of oxygen; Reduction = gain of electrons/loss of oxygen (always happen together — redox). Catalyst = speeds up reaction without being consumed.
Common reaction fact: Sodium bicarbonate heated strongly → Sodium Carbonate + water + CO₂.

Common alloys: Steel = Iron+Carbon | Brass = Copper+Zinc | Bronze = Copper+Tin | Alnico = Aluminium+Nickel+Cobalt (used in magnets) | Stainless Steel = Iron+Chromium+Nickel.
Extraction of metals: Ore → concentration → reduction (smelting) → refining. E.g. Cinnabar (HgS) is the ore of Mercury. Cassiterite is the ore of Tin.
Noble/Inert gases: Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, Radon — full outer electron shell, very unreactive.
Valency: The combining power of an element, based on electrons in outermost shell.

Radioactivity: Alpha particles (2 protons+2 neutrons, +charge, repel each other via Coulomb/electrostatic force), Beta particles (electrons), Gamma rays (pure energy, no charge).
Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment: Used gold because it can be beaten into extremely thin sheets (malleable) — proved atoms are mostly empty space with a dense positive nucleus.

Periodic Table basics: Arranged by atomic number (protons). Groups (vertical) = similar properties; Periods (horizontal) = same number of shells. Metals (left side, malleable, conduct) vs Non-metals (right side, brittle, poor conductors) vs Metalloids (in between).

Valency: The combining power of an element, based on electrons in outermost shell.

Acids: All acids contain Hydrogen (H⁺ ions); turn blue litmus red; pH < 7. Common: HCl (stomach), Citric acid (citrus fruits), Acetic/Ethanoic acid (vinegar).

pH scale: 0–14; 7 = neutral (pure water); below 7 = acidic; above 7 = basic.
Reaction types: Oxidation = loss of electrons/gain of oxygen; Reduction = gain of electrons/loss of oxygen (always happen together — redox). Catalyst = speeds up reaction without being consumed.
Common reaction fact: Sodium bicarbonate heated strongly → Sodium Carbonate + water + CO₂.

Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

questions.q: The rate of oxygen diffusion is extremely near to _______, if the temperature of both the helium and oxygen gases is the same.
questions.theory:
Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).
Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

Acids: All acids contain Hydrogen (H⁺ ions); turn blue litmus red; pH < 7. Common: HCl (stomach), Citric acid (citrus fruits), Acetic/Ethanoic acid (vinegar).

Common reaction fact: Sodium bicarbonate heated strongly → Sodium Carbonate + water + CO₂.

Refraction: Light bends when passing between different media (different densities) — causes a straw to look 'bent' in water.

Atomic structure: Nucleus (protons + neutrons, together called nucleons) at center; Electrons orbit around it. Proton = +charge, Electron = −charge, Neutron = no charge.
Isotopes: Same element (same protons), different number of neutrons → different atomic mass. E.g. Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37.
Radioactivity: Alpha particles (2 protons+2 neutrons, +charge, repel each other via Coulomb/electrostatic force), Beta particles (electrons), Gamma rays (pure energy, no charge).
Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment: Used gold because it can be beaten into extremely thin sheets (malleable) — proved atoms are mostly empty space with a dense positive nucleus.

questions.q: The tube light is usually full of ………… gas.

Reflection: Light bounces off a surface, stays in same medium (mirrors).
Refraction: Light bends when passing between different media (different densities) — causes a straw to look 'bent' in water.
Lenses: Convex (converging, thicker middle — magnifying glass); Concave (diverging, thinner middle — used in spectacles for myopia).

questions.q: Frequency of vibrations is usually expressed in the terms of which among the following?
questions.theory:
Sound waves: Longitudinal waves (particles vibrate parallel to wave direction) — needs a medium, can't travel in vacuum.
Key terms: Frequency (pitch, Hz), Amplitude (loudness), Wavelength (distance between two compressions or two rarefactions).
Compression & Rarefaction: Compression = particles pushed close together (high pressure); Rarefaction = particles spread apart (low pressure) — sound travels as alternating C-R pairs.
Echo: Reflection of sound off a hard surface, heard after the original sound.

Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).

Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

questions.q: How much force is required to lift a mass of 100g?
questions.theory:
Core formulas: Force = mass × acceleration (F=ma) | Weight = mass × gravity (W=mg) | Density = mass/volume | Pressure = Force/Area | Work = Force × distance | Power = Work/time.
Newton's Laws: 1st (Inertia) — object stays at rest/motion unless force acts. 2nd — F=ma. 3rd — every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
Speed vs Velocity: Speed = scalar (distance/time). Velocity = vector (displacement/time, has direction).
Simple machines: Lever, Pulley, Wheel & Axle, Inclined Plane, Screw, Wedge — all reduce effort needed to do work.
Friction: Opposes relative motion between surfaces; static friction > kinetic friction.
Units: Force = Newton (N), Work/Energy = Joule (J), Power = Watt (W), Pressure = Pascal (Pa).

questions.q: Transfer of heat in liquids and gases takes place by
questions.theory:
Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).
Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

questions.theory:
Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).
Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

questions.q: Which colour has the shortest wavelength out of the following?
questions.theory:
Reflection: Light bounces off a surface, stays in same medium (mirrors).
Refraction: Light bends when passing between different media (different densities) — causes a straw to look 'bent' in water.
Lenses: Convex (converging, thicker middle — magnifying glass); Concave (diverging, thinner middle — used in spectacles for myopia).
Prism & Spectrum: A prism splits white light into 7 colours (VIBGYOR: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) because each colour bends by a different amount (different wavelengths).
Mirrors: Plane (flat, same-size image), Concave (converging, used in torches/headlights), Convex (diverging, used in vehicle side mirrors for wider view).

Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).
Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

questions.q: The appearance of sound to a human ear is objectively characterised by which of the following parameters? 1. Frequency 2. Intensity 3. Waveform Choose the correct code
questions.theory:
Sound waves: Longitudinal waves (particles vibrate parallel to wave direction) — needs a medium, can't travel in vacuum.
Key terms: Frequency (pitch, Hz), Amplitude (loudness), Wavelength (distance between two compressions or two rarefactions).
Compression & Rarefaction: Compression = particles pushed close together (high pressure); Rarefaction = particles spread apart (low pressure) — sound travels as alternating C-R pairs.
Echo: Reflection of sound off a hard surface, heard after the original sound.

Conductors vs Insulators: Conductors allow current flow (metals, e.g. copper); Insulators block it (rubber, plastic); Semiconductors (silicon) behave as either depending on conditions.
Circuit types: Series (one path, current same everywhere, resistances add up) vs Parallel (multiple paths, voltage same across each branch).
Magnetism: Like poles repel, unlike poles attract. Electromagnetic induction = moving a magnet near a coil generates current.

questions.q: What is the cause of ozone depletion?
questions.theory:
Food chain: Producers (plants, make own food) → Primary consumers (herbivores, eat plants) → Secondary consumers (carnivores, eat herbivores) → Decomposers (bacteria/fungi, break down dead matter).
Greenhouse Effect: Earth's atmosphere traps heat (via gases like CO₂, methane, water vapour), warming the surface — natural process, but human activity intensifies it (global warming).
Key environmental gases: Ozone (O₃, protects from UV, layer in stratosphere; CFCs deplete it) | Methane (from landfills/cattle, potent greenhouse gas) | Carbon Monoxide (from vehicle exhaust/burning, NOT wood products naturally).
Waste: Biodegradable (decomposes naturally, e.g. food waste) vs Non-biodegradable (plastic, metal — doesn't decompose easily). MSW = Municipal Solid Waste.
Major Indian environmental programs: Namami Gange (cleaning Ganga), Swachh Bharat (sanitation), National programs tied to Wildlife Protection Act 1972.
Renewable vs Non-renewable: Renewable = replenishes naturally (solar, wind, hydro). Non-renewable = finite (coal, petroleum, natural gas).

questions.q: Soil develops slowly in which season or temperature?
questions.theory:
Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).
Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

Isotopes: Same element (same protons), different number of neutrons → different atomic mass. E.g. Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37.
Radioactivity: Alpha particles (2 protons+2 neutrons, +charge, repel each other via Coulomb/electrostatic force), Beta particles (electrons), Gamma rays (pure energy, no charge).
Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment: Used gold because it can be beaten into extremely thin sheets (malleable) — proved atoms are mostly empty space with a dense positive nucleus.

Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).
Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

Sound waves: Longitudinal waves (particles vibrate parallel to wave direction) — needs a medium, can't travel in vacuum.
Key terms: Frequency (pitch, Hz), Amplitude (loudness), Wavelength (distance between two compressions or two rarefactions).
Compression & Rarefaction: Compression = particles pushed close together (high pressure); Rarefaction = particles spread apart (low pressure) — sound travels as alternating C-R pairs.
Echo: Reflection of sound off a hard surface, heard after the original sound.

Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).
Boiling point vs Melting point: Boiling = liquid→gas; Melting = solid→liquid. Both are constant for a pure substance at fixed pressure.
Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

Common alloys: Steel = Iron+Carbon | Brass = Copper+Zinc | Bronze = Copper+Tin | Alnico = Aluminium+Nickel+Cobalt (used in magnets) | Stainless Steel = Iron+Chromium+Nickel.

Noble/Inert gases: Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, Radon — full outer electron shell, very unreactive.
Valency: The combining power of an element, based on electrons in outermost shell.

Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).

Specific heat capacity: Amount of heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — water has unusually high specific heat (that's why it heats/cools slowly).

questions.q: Which of the following is not an acid base indicator?

Acids: All acids contain Hydrogen (H⁺ ions); turn blue litmus red; pH < 7. Common: HCl (stomach), Citric acid (citrus fruits), Acetic/Ethanoic acid (vinegar).
Bases/Alkalis: Turn red litmus blue; pH > 7; release OH⁻ ions. Common: NaOH (caustic soda), baking soda (sodium bicarbonate, mild base).
pH scale: 0–14; 7 = neutral (pure water); below 7 = acidic; above 7 = basic.
Reaction types: Oxidation = loss of electrons/gain of oxygen; Reduction = gain of electrons/loss of oxygen (always happen together — redox). Catalyst = speeds up reaction without being consumed.
Common reaction fact: Sodium bicarbonate heated strongly → Sodium Carbonate + water + CO₂.

questions.q: What causes a glowing bulb to heat up?
questions.theory:
Heat vs Temperature: Heat = total thermal energy transferred (Joules); Temperature = degree of hotness/coldness, average kinetic energy of particles (°C/K).
Modes of heat transfer: Conduction (through solids, direct contact), Convection (through fluids — liquid/gas, via currents), Radiation (through empty space, e.g. sunlight — no medium needed).

questions.q: The kind of bonding in the molecule of HCl is _________.
questions.theory:
Acids: All acids contain Hydrogen (H⁺ ions); turn blue litmus red; pH < 7. Common: HCl (stomach), Citric acid (citrus fruits), Acetic/Ethanoic acid (vinegar).
Bases/Alkalis: Turn red litmus blue; pH > 7; release OH⁻ ions. Common: NaOH (caustic soda), baking soda (sodium bicarbonate, mild base).
pH scale: 0–14; 7 = neutral (pure water); below 7 = acidic; above 7 = basic.
Reaction types: Oxidation = loss of electrons/gain of oxygen; Reduction = gain of electrons/loss of oxygen (always happen together — redox). Catalyst = speeds up reaction without being consumed.
Common reaction fact: Sodium bicarbonate heated strongly → Sodium Carbonate + water + CO₂.

Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + sunlight → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + 6O₂, occurs in chloroplast (contains chlorophyll, the green pigment that absorbs light).
Plant parts: Root (absorbs water/minerals, anchors plant), Stem (support, transport via xylem-water/phloem-food), Leaf (photosynthesis site), Flower (reproduction).
Macro-nutrients for plants: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K) — the 'NPK' in fertilizers; plus Calcium, Magnesium, Sulphur.
Plant classification: Bryophytes (non-vascular, e.g. moss) → Pteridophytes (vascular, no seeds, e.g. fern) → Gymnosperms (naked seeds, e.g. pine) → Angiosperms (flowering, covered seeds).
Storage forms: Onion stores food as modified leaves (bulb); many plants store carbohydrates as starch; algae store as laminarin/mannitol.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the electron is incorrect?
questions.a: The mass of the electron is equal to the mass of the neutron
questions.theory:
Atomic structure: Nucleus (protons + neutrons, together called nucleons) at center; Electrons orbit around it. Proton = +charge, Electron = −charge, Neutron = no charge.
Isotopes: Same element (same protons), different number of neutrons → different atomic mass. E.g. Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37.
Radioactivity: Alpha particles (2 protons+2 neutrons, +charge, repel each other via Coulomb/electrostatic force), Beta particles (electrons), Gamma rays (pure energy, no charge).
Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment: Used gold because it can be beaten into extremely thin sheets (malleable) — proved atoms are mostly empty space with a dense positive nucleus.

questions.theory:
Ohm's Law: V = IR (Voltage = Current × Resistance).
Conductors vs Insulators: Conductors allow current flow (metals, e.g. copper); Insulators block it (rubber, plastic); Semiconductors (silicon) behave as either depending on conditions.
Circuit types: Series (one path, current same everywhere, resistances add up) vs Parallel (multiple paths, voltage same across each branch).
Magnetism: Like poles repel, unlike poles attract. Electromagnetic induction = moving a magnet near a coil generates current.
Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Used to find the direction of Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (motor effect).

Food chain: Producers (plants, make own food) → Primary consumers (herbivores, eat plants) → Secondary consumers (carnivores, eat herbivores) → Decomposers (bacteria/fungi, break down dead matter).
Greenhouse Effect: Earth's atmosphere traps heat (via gases like CO₂, methane, water vapour), warming the surface — natural process, but human activity intensifies it (global warming).
Key environmental gases: Ozone (O₃, protects from UV, layer in stratosphere; CFCs deplete it) | Methane (from landfills/cattle, potent greenhouse gas) | Carbon Monoxide (from vehicle exhaust/burning, NOT wood products naturally).
Waste: Biodegradable (decomposes naturally, e.g. food waste) vs Non-biodegradable (plastic, metal — doesn't decompose easily). MSW = Municipal Solid Waste.
Major Indian environmental programs: Namami Gange (cleaning Ganga), Swachh Bharat (sanitation), National programs tied to Wildlife Protection Act 1972.
Renewable vs Non-renewable: Renewable = replenishes naturally (solar, wind, hydro). Non-renewable = finite (coal, petroleum, natural gas).

Sound waves: Longitudinal waves (particles vibrate parallel to wave direction) — needs a medium, can't travel in vacuum.
Key terms: Frequency (pitch, Hz), Amplitude (loudness), Wavelength (distance between two compressions or two rarefactions).

Echo: Reflection of sound off a hard surface, heard after the original sound.

Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + sunlight → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + 6O₂, occurs in chloroplast (contains chlorophyll, the green pigment that absorbs light).

Macro-nutrients for plants: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K) — the 'NPK' in fertilizers; plus Calcium, Magnesium, Sulphur.
Plant classification: Bryophytes (non-vascular, e.g. moss) → Pteridophytes (vascular, no seeds, e.g. fern) → Gymnosperms (naked seeds, e.g. pine) → Angiosperms (flowering, covered seeds).
Storage forms: Onion stores food as modified leaves (bulb); many plants store carbohydrates as starch; algae store as laminarin/mannitol.

Refraction: Light bends when passing between different media (different densities) — causes a straw to look 'bent' in water.
Lenses: Convex (converging, thicker middle — magnifying glass); Concave (diverging, thinner middle — used in spectacles for myopia).

Mirrors: Plane (flat, same-size image), Concave (converging, used in torches/headlights), Convex (diverging, used in vehicle side mirrors for wider view).

questions.q: The electronic configuration of chlorine is:
questions.theory:
Atomic structure: Nucleus (protons + neutrons, together called nucleons) at center; Electrons orbit around it. Proton = +charge, Electron = −charge, Neutron = no charge.
Isotopes: Same element (same protons), different number of neutrons → different atomic mass. E.g. Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37.
Radioactivity: Alpha particles (2 protons+2 neutrons, +charge, repel each other via Coulomb/electrostatic force), Beta particles (electrons), Gamma rays (pure energy, no charge).
Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment: Used gold because it can be beaten into extremely thin sheets (malleable) — proved atoms are mostly empty space with a dense positive nucleus.

questions.q: What is the name of the law that states that the current flowing through a conductor is directly
questions.theory:
Ohm's Law: V = IR (Voltage = Current × Resistance).
Conductors vs Insulators: Conductors allow current flow (metals, e.g. copper); Insulators block it (rubber, plastic); Semiconductors (silicon) behave as either depending on conditions.
Circuit types: Series (one path, current same everywhere, resistances add up) vs Parallel (multiple paths, voltage same across each branch).
Magnetism: Like poles repel, unlike poles attract. Electromagnetic induction = moving a magnet near a coil generates current.
Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Used to find the direction of Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (motor effect).

Cell: Basic unit of life. Nucleus = control center (has DNA); Mitochondria = 'powerhouse' (makes energy/ATP); Ribosomes = protein synthesis.
Organ systems: Digestive (mouth→esophagus→stomach→small intestine→large intestine), Respiratory (nose→trachea→lungs, gas exchange in alveoli), Circulatory (heart pumps blood via arteries=away from heart, veins=towards heart), Nervous (brain+spinal cord+nerves; neuron = nerve cell, synapse = junction between neurons).
Vitamin deficiency diseases (high-yield): A→Night blindness | B1→Beriberi | B3→Pellagra | B12→Anemia | C→Scurvy | D→Rickets(children)/Osteomalacia(adults) | K→Poor blood clotting.
Blood: RBC (carries oxygen via haemoglobin), WBC (fights infection), Platelets (clotting). Blood groups: A, B, AB, O (based on antigens).
Common disease-causing agents: Rabies→bite of infected animal (dog); Malaria→Anopheles mosquito (Plasmodium parasite); Dengue/Chikungunya→Aedes mosquito; TB→bacteria (lungs); Filariasis→Wuchereria bancrofti.
Hormones: Insulin (pancreas, controls blood sugar), Thyroxine (thyroid, metabolism), Adrenaline (adrenal, fight-or-flight), Growth hormone (pituitary).

questions.q: The term used for wind pollination is ________.
questions.theory:
Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + sunlight → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + 6O₂, occurs in chloroplast (contains chlorophyll, the green pigment that absorbs light).
Plant parts: Root (absorbs water/minerals, anchors plant), Stem (support, transport via xylem-water/phloem-food), Leaf (photosynthesis site), Flower (reproduction).
Macro-nutrients for plants: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K) — the 'NPK' in fertilizers; plus Calcium, Magnesium, Sulphur.
Plant classification: Bryophytes (non-vascular, e.g. moss) → Pteridophytes (vascular, no seeds, e.g. fern) → Gymnosperms (naked seeds, e.g. pine) → Angiosperms (flowering, covered seeds).
Storage forms: Onion stores food as modified leaves (bulb); many plants store carbohydrates as starch; algae store as laminarin/mannitol.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an essential plant nutrient element?
questions.theory:
Periodic Table basics: Arranged by atomic number (protons). Groups (vertical) = similar properties; Periods (horizontal) = same number of shells. Metals (left side, malleable, conduct) vs Non-metals (right side, brittle, poor conductors) vs Metalloids (in between).
Common alloys: Steel = Iron+Carbon | Brass = Copper+Zinc | Bronze = Copper+Tin | Alnico = Aluminium+Nickel+Cobalt (used in magnets) | Stainless Steel = Iron+Chromium+Nickel.
Extraction of metals: Ore → concentration → reduction (smelting) → refining. E.g. Cinnabar (HgS) is the ore of Mercury. Cassiterite is the ore of Tin.
Noble/Inert gases: Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, Radon — full outer electron shell, very unreactive.
Valency: The combining power of an element, based on electrons in outermost shell.

questions.q: Which of the following contributes maximum to the greenhouse effect?
questions.theory:
Food chain: Producers (plants, make own food) → Primary consumers (herbivores, eat plants) → Secondary consumers (carnivores, eat herbivores) → Decomposers (bacteria/fungi, break down dead matter).
Greenhouse Effect: Earth's atmosphere traps heat (via gases like CO₂, methane, water vapour), warming the surface — natural process, but human activity intensifies it (global warming).
Key environmental gases: Ozone (O₃, protects from UV, layer in stratosphere; CFCs deplete it) | Methane (from landfills/cattle, potent greenhouse gas) | Carbon Monoxide (from vehicle exhaust/burning, NOT wood products naturally).
Waste: Biodegradable (decomposes naturally, e.g. food waste) vs Non-biodegradable (plastic, metal — doesn't decompose easily). MSW = Municipal Solid Waste.
Major Indian environmental programs: Namami Gange (cleaning Ganga), Swachh Bharat (sanitation), National programs tied to Wildlife Protection Act 1972.
Renewable vs Non-renewable: Renewable = replenishes naturally (solar, wind, hydro). Non-renewable = finite (coal, petroleum, natural gas).
